summary: Rudolf Otto was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied at Erlangen-Nuremberg, Göttingen, and Tübingen under Richard von Garbe. He held posts in theology at Göttingen and Breslau before serving as professor at Marburg from 1917 to 1929.

Rudolf Otto Franke worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen and Bonn under August Fick and Franz Kielhorn, later lecturing as Privatdozent at Berlin before serving as professor at the University of Königsberg from 1895 to 1927.
Rudolf Seydel worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Leipzig from around 1852 to 1856 and later held a post there from circa 1860 to 1892.
Rudolf Steiner worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at TU Wien and the University of Rostock, and held a post at the Goethe and Schiller Archives from around 1890 to 1896.

Rudolf Stübe worked in religious studies. Between 1890 and 1894, he studied at the University of Rostock, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, where he earned his Ph.D. under Richard Pischel.

Rudolf Thomas Siegfried specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and in Berlin under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber, later serving as Lecturer in Sanskrit at Trinity College Dublin from 1858 to 1862.

Rudolf Thurneysen was a linguist who studied at Basel, Leipzig under Ernst Windisch, Berlin under Heinrich Zimmer, and Paris under Henri Gaidoz. He held posts at Jena, Freiburg (1887–1913), and Bonn (1913–1923).

Rudolf Westphal worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Marburg under Johann Gildemeister and at Tübingen. He held posts at Tübingen, Breslau (1857–1862), Fellin Landesschule, Goldingen Gymnasium, and the Katkov Lyceum (1875–1881).

Rudolf von Roth was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tübinger Stift under Heinrich Ewald and in Paris under Eugène Burnouf. He spent his career at the University of Tübingen, serving as Extraordinarius from 1848 to 1895.

Rudolph Rahmann studied at Missionshaus St. Gabriel and the University of Vienna under Wilhelm Schmidt and Wilhelm Koppers. He held posts at Fu Jen Catholic University, the University of San Carlos, and the University of Fribourg (1956–1960).

Rudrapatna Shamasastry worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Sri Chamarajendra Sanskrit College, University of Madras, Oriental University, and University of Calcutta, and served at Sri Chamarajendra Samskrita Maha Patashala, Oriental Research Institute Mysore, and Mysore Archaeological Department.

Ruixuan Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Leiden University under Paul Harrison, Jens-Uwe Hartmann, and others, and is attested as a faculty member at Peking University in 2026.
Rulon Wells was a scholar of linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Utah and Harvard University, and held a post at Yale University from circa 1945 to 1989.
Rune Edvin Arvid Johansson worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Ceylon and Lund University, where he also served as a lecturer.

Rupert Gethin specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his BA and PhD at the University of Manchester under Lance S. Cousins, and held long-term posts at the University of Bristol beginning in 1987.

Ruriko Sakuma specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She studied at Nagoya University and has held posts at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Ruth Fuller Sasaki was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at the University of Chicago and under teachers including D. T. Suzuki. She served as director of the First Zen Institute of America and abbess of Ryōsen-an.

Ruth Gamble works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at RMIT and the Australian National University, and held research and teaching posts at ANU, the University of Munich, and La Trobe University.
Ruth Norton Albright was an Indologist who completed her PhD at Johns Hopkins University between circa 1916 and 1921, studying under Maurice Bloomfield.

Ruth W. Dunnell is a scholar of Sinology, history/archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned her PhD at Princeton University, studied under Jinbo Shi, and served as James P. Storer Associate Professor of Asian History at Kenyon College.
